docs.title: Commit record and trace schema
docs.text:
A commit record's JSON form (CommitRecord.to_json()) is a document of the commit record schema. A trace is a JSON Lines file: a header line of the trace header schema, then one commit record per word. Download the schema files to validate either with any JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) validator.

IPU commit record, version 1.0.0 (commit_record.v1.json): One retired VLIW word (E04-29). Integers up to 32 bits are JSON numbers; wider data are lowercase hex strings, little-endian. Register names are ipu_isa's. NOP slots are omitted. A write is a range the word wrote, with its value at the end of the cycle. A faulting word has no effect (precise faults), so a fault record has no writes.

Field Type Required Meaning cycle integer (≥ 0) yes Records before this one in the trace. pc_before integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The word's PC. pc_after integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The PC of the next word. slots array of object yes The word's ops, one per non-NOP slot. slots[].slot string yes The slot, as ipu_isa.slots names it. slots[].mnemonic string yes The op's mnemonic. slots[].fields object of integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The encoded operand values, by operand name. slots[].tag "emulator" no Present only on an op with no hardware equivalent. reg_writes array of object yes The registers the word wrote, at their end-of-cycle values. reg_writes[].register string yes The bank, as ipu_isa.registers names it. reg_writes[].index integer (≥ 0) yes, in form 1 of 2 A scalar register (lr, cr): the register within the bank. reg_writes[].value integer (0 to 4294967295) yes, in form 1 of 2 A scalar register: its unsigned 32-bit value. reg_writes[].tag "emulator" no Present only on a register with no hardware equivalent (wide-vector debug). reg_writes[].offset integer (≥ 0) yes, in form 2 of 2 A vector register: the first byte written, within the bank. reg_writes[].data string (^([0-9a-f]{2})*$) yes, in form 2 of 2 A vector register: the bytes written. xmem_writes array of object yes The XMEM ranges the word wrote. xmem_writes[].address integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The first XMEM byte written. xmem_writes[].data string (^([0-9a-f]{2})*$) yes The bytes written. outcome one of "retired", "break", "halt", "fault" yes break: the word's BREAK slot fired, and the word retired when the run went on. halt: a HALT word retired. fault: the word faulted (fault says which). fault null or object yes The fault the word raised, or null. fault.id string (^F-[1-9]$) yes The fault ID, as the fault list writes it. fault.pc integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The faulting word's PC. arith_events array of string yes Arithmetic events of the word (E04-23); empty until they are modelled.
  • When outcome is "fault": fault is an object, reg_writes is empty, xmem_writes is empty. Otherwise fault is null.

IPU trace header, version 1.0.0 (trace.v1.json): A trace is JSON Lines: this header on the first line, then one commit record (commit_record schema) per line (E04-29).

Field Type Required Meaning schema_version string (^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$) yes The commit record schema's version. isa_digest string (^[0-9a-f]{64}$) yes SHA-256 of the ISA definition (ipu_isa.trace_schema.isa_digest). format string yes The element format the program ran in. program_digest string (^[0-9a-f]{64}$) yes SHA-256 of the program as it is loaded: each IMEM word up to the program length, packed little-endian in its emulator word width (ipu_isa.codec.word.word_bytes()), an empty word as zeros. emulator_version string yes The version of the model that wrote the trace (ipu_emu.trace.EMULATOR_VERSION for this emulator).

arith_events holds the names of ipu_isa.faults.ArithmeticEvent: acc_overflow, nan_result, quant_saturation, sorted. An event never halts the model.

docs.title: Faults
docs.text:
A faulting word's commit record has outcome fault and names the fault in fault.id; status.fault is the same fault as a FaultId. These are the IDs of the fault list; the emulator section of Faults says what the model checks for each.

ID FaultId Fault Detected in In the model F-1 FaultId.F1 A slot holds a reserved opcode or a reserved operand encoding. ctrl Reported. F-2 FaultId.F2 CTRL fetches at a PC at or beyond the program length, by sequential flow, branch or BR. ctrl Reported. F-3 FaultId.F3 Two LR lanes of one word write the same LR. ctrl Reported. F-4 FaultId.F4 The index of LD.MULT.CYCLIC is not 0, 128, 256 or 384. ctrl Reported. F-5 FaultId.F5 ACC.RESHAPE has a mask above 8, or a participating source or destination index of 128 or more. ctrl Reported. F-6 FaultId.F6 A load or a store addresses a table that is not configured, or a row beyond the table size. cache_agent Reported. F-7 FaultId.F7 A load addresses a write-only table, or a store addresses a read-only table. cache_agent Never raised: the emulator has no table configuration, so no table is read-only or write-only. F-8 FaultId.F8 A word stalls for longer than a programmable limit. cache_agent Not modelled: never reported; the emulator has no stall model (OQ-28). F-9 FaultId.F9 A kernel runs for more cycles than a programmable limit. ctrl Reported.

docs.title: Conformance suite
docs.text:
src/ipu-isa/conformance/ holds the ISA's expected behaviour as data: for each case a program (program.asm, program.bin), its starting state (setup.json, schema setup.schema.json) and the trace of its run (expected.trace.jsonl). No case contains Python, so another implementation (the RTL under cocotb, another model) needs only these files and the schemas.

To run the suite against another implementation, for each case:

  1. Skip it if setup.json has "emulator_only": true.
  2. Reset in the case's format and load program.bin.
  3. Zero every register and XMEM byte (CR0 and CR1 aside), then write the registers and XMEM regions of setup.json and set its fault enables.
  4. Run until HALT, a fault or max_cycles, recording a commit record per word.
  5. Compare the header's schema_version, isa_digest, format and program_digest with the expected trace's, then each record, field by field.

The suite's README.md has the details of each step. bazel test //src/ipu-emu:test_conformance runs every case through this API.

docs.title: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE in the emulator
docs.text:
The AaQ stage spec describes how the hardware applies an activation: a function id (for example from act_cr_idx and a CR read) and α-like parameters that are not VLIW immediates. They come from implementation-defined configuration (constants, fuses, side-band registers).

The Python emulator adds an AAQ-slot instruction, ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, that applies one of thirteen activation shapes to the elements of R_ACC and writes the results to POST_AAQ_REG, without modelling the act_cr_idx path. It is a placeholder until the AaQ stage is specified (OQ-20).

ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu CR15;;
  • Syntax: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE activation_fn cr_idx. activation_fn is a keyword: identity, relu, relu6, sigmoid, tanh, gelu, softplus, elu, exp2, reciprocal, rsqrt, silu or window. The number of active elements is cr_idx's valid_elements, the same dstructure field the AGG.* instructions read (Configuration registers). cr_idx is required: any of CR0–CR15, with no default.
  • Where it is defined: the keyword order is the ISA's ActivationFn operand, ACTIVATION_FN_NAMES in src/ipu-isa/src/ipu_isa/activations.py. The math is the emulator's apply_activation in src/ipu-emu/src/ipu_emu/activations.py.

docs.title: R_ACC, POST_AAQ_REG and ST.AAQ
docs.text:
• Accumulation stays in R_ACC: 512 bytes, 128 32-bit elements. AGG.SUM, AGG.SUM.FIRST, AGG.MAX and AGG.MAX.FIRST reduce R_ACC in place and write one R_ACC element, chosen by an LR.
  • ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE reads R_ACC, applies the activation to each active element and writes the result to POST_AAQ_REG. R_ACC is unchanged.
  • POST_AAQ_REG is, for now, a 512-byte staging register with the same element layout as R_ACC.
  • Activation and quantization are one instruction; there is no activate-only or quantize-only opcode. In INT8 the activated elements are clamped to [-128, 127] and written as 128 bytes at the start of POST_AAQ_REG; the rest is zeroed. In FP32 and INT32 the activated 32-bit elements are written whole, and quantized to that 128-byte prefix only when AaqOptions.quantize_output is set (IpuState(aaq=AaqOptions(quantize_output=True))). The 8-bit float formats refuse it.
  • ST.AAQ stores all 512 bytes of POST_AAQ_REG to XMEM, in whatever layout it holds when the store issues.

docs.title: α and the window bounds (elu, window)
docs.text:
The ISA has no operand for elu's α or for the bounds of window. The emulator reads them from the state's activation field, an ActivationParams (elu_alpha, window_a, window_b). Unset, they take the defaults in ipu_emu/activations.py (DEFAULT_ELU_ALPHA, DEFAULT_WINDOW_A, DEFAULT_WINDOW_B).

window is the half-open indicator: window(x) = 1 for a <= x < b, else 0. The defaults are placeholders until calibration: a = 0.0, b = 0.1. On the hardware, window belongs to the LUT-backed activation group of the AaQ spec, so a and b are part of the loaded LUT; the emulator keeps them on the state instead.

They are set on the state, like the element format, not through a CR:

from ipu_emu.activations import ActivationParams
from ipu_emu.ipu_state import IpuState

state = IpuState(activation=ActivationParams(elu_alpha=1.0, window_a=0.0, window_b=0.1))
# or, after construction:
state.set_activation_alphas(elu_alpha=1.0, window_a=0.0, window_b=0.1)

A state keeps its values from run to run; change them with set_activation_alphas, or build a new IpuState.

docs.title: Assembly Language Syntax
docs.text: The IPU assembler is a Python-based tool that turns assembly source into binary VLIW instructions for the emulator. Instruction names, operands, and encoding are driven by instruction_spec.py in ipu_isa; the Instruction reference and Operand types are generated from that same toolchain.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Jinja2 preprocessing — templates and macros for generated assembly
  • Label resolution — forward and backward references
  • VLIW compounds — multiple pipeline slots per cycle (COND, LR×3, LOAD, MULT, ACC, AAQ, STORE; emulator-only: ACC_STORE, BREAK)
  • Syntax validation — Lark-based parser with detailed errors

docs.title: Basic Syntax
docs.text:
Assembly is line-oriented. One compound instruction may contain several slot instructions separated by ;, terminated by ;;.

# Comments start with # or //
label:                          # Labels end with a colon
    LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;           # LOAD: load into mult stage R0
    MULT.RC.VV LR1 R0 0 LR3 CR15; # MULT: element-wise multiply
    ACC.ADD;                      # ACC: accumulate
    INC LR0 1;                    # LR: bump address (increment via INC)
    BNE LR0 LR1 next;             # COND: branch
    ;;
next:
    HALT;;

By convention, instruction mnemonics are written in upper case in documentation and examples (e.g. MULT.RC.VV, LD.MULT). Register names are written in upper case (LR0, R0, CR0); operand placeholders such as dest are lower case. The assembler accepts any case for mnemonics and register tokens.

docs.title: Compound instructions
docs.text:
A full IPU instruction is one compound word: several slots execute in parallel in a single cycle.

Pattern:

load_inst; mult_inst; acc_inst; aaq_inst; store_inst; acc_store_inst; lr_inst_a; lr_inst_b; lr_inst_c; cond_inst; break_inst;;

Rules:

  • Each slot appears a fixed number of times (see SLOT_COUNT in instruction_spec.py); unused slots are filled with that slot’s NOP by the assembler.
  • Slot order in the binary word (MSB → LSB) is defined by the toolchain: cond, three lr sub-slots, load, mult, acc, aaq, store, acc_store, break (see the layout diagram on the Instruction reference).
  • The slots of one word execute in a fixed order, and each register read sees either the value at cycle start or the value forwarded from an earlier slot of the same word: see Execution order and timing.
  • The emulator-only slots (ACC_STORE, BREAK) are not implemented in real IPU hardware: see the instruction format.

Example (parallel slots):

loop:
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0; MULT.RC.VV LR1 R0 0 LR3 CR15; ACC.ADD; INC LR0 1; BNE LR0 LR1 loop;;

docs.title: Register names
docs.text:
The mult-stage and scalar register tokens below are derived from REGISTER_DEFINITIONS in ipu_isa.registers (same source as the assembler).

Kind Assembler tokens Notes Mult stage R0, R1 128-byte vectors; 2-bit mult-stage field (2 reserved). See MultStageReg. Cyclic / mask (architectural) Cyclic (RC) and mask (RM) register files are documented per instruction in the reference; operands pass byte offsets via LR values. Loop / scalar LR0–LR15 General-purpose; read/write. See LrIdx. Constant CR0–CR15 Read-only in assembly; the host writes CR2–CR15 before a kernel runs. CR0 and CR1 are the read-only constants 0 and 1 (see Configuration registers). CR15 conventionally holds dstructure configuration (see DstructureCrIdx) but is a valid CrIdx/LcrIdx operand like any other CR. See CrIdx.

The mem_bypass vector may still exist in the emulator regfile for debugging, but it is not a valid mult-stage assembly operand.

LR slot: SET copies from a CR register (see CrIdx); ADD/SUB's src_b is register-only (see LcrIdx) — use INC/DEC for an immediate operand instead (see LrIncDecImmediate); INC.MODP2 uses a dedicated k immediate (see LrModPow2KImmediate).

docs.title: Labels and branches
docs.text:
start:
    SET LR0 CR0;;
loop:
    INC LR0 1;;
    BNE LR0 LR1 loop;;
    HALT;;

Relative labels such as B +5 / B -2 are supported where the grammar accepts a label token (see cond-slot instructions in the reference).

docs.title: Local labels
docs.text:
A label made of decimal digits only, such as 1:, is a local label (the GNU assembler's numeric labels). It may be defined any number of times. 1f refers to the next 1: after the current instruction word, and 1b to the nearest 1: at or before it, so a word may branch to its own label with 1b. A bare 1 as a branch target is an error. Local labels let a macro or a loop body use one short label in every expansion:

{% macro count_to(limit_cr) %}
    SET LR0 CR0;;
1:
    INC LR0 1;;
    BNE LR0 {{ limit_cr }} 1b;;
{% endmacro %}
{{ count_to("CR2") }}
{{ count_to("CR3") }}
    HALT;;

docs.title: Execution order and timing
docs.text:
This section is generated from ipu_isa.timing and the register accesses each instruction declares in instruction_spec.py.

The slots of one instruction word execute in this order: BREAK → LR → LOAD → MULT → ACC → AAQ → STORE → ACC_STORE → COND. BREAK is evaluated before any slot writes (it may halt the word); the LR sub-slots all read before any of them writes.

A register read sees one of two values: the value at cycle start (when the word began), or the forwarded value (after the writes of earlier slots of the same word). The timing contract is four rules:

  1. The Control stage (LR, COND) reads LRs at cycle start; every other stage reads LRs after the LR writes of the same word.
  2. MULT reads R0, R1, R_CYCLIC and R_MASK at cycle start.
  3. MULT_RES is forwarded to ACC (including AGG and RESHAPE); R_ACC is forwarded to AAQ.
  4. LR sub-slots read cycle-start values.

Any other read is forwarded when every slot that writes the register runs earlier in the word, and at cycle start otherwise. CRs are never written during a run, so CR reads are at cycle start.

The timing model explains the rules, with an example of each.

docs.title: Known deviations
docs.text: None: every read in the emulator follows the contract.

docs.title: Masking
docs.text: Multiply instructions (MULT.RC.VV, MULT.RC.VE, MULT.RC.VS, MULT.VE, MULT.EE) support element masking: after the multiply, elements in MULT_RES whose corresponding mask bit is 1 are active and pass through to accumulation; elements whose bit is 0 are zeroed (deactivated). A mask of all-ones leaves every element active (the reset default); a mask of all-zeros deactivates every element.

docs.title: R_MASK register
docs.text:
R_MASK is a 128-byte register packed as 8 independent 128-bit slots (slots 0–7). Load it from XMEM with:

LD.MASK offset base;;

offset is an LR register holding the XMEM byte offset; base is a CR register holding the base address. The full 1024-bit register is always overwritten in one cycle. A multiply reads R_MASK at cycle start, so an LD.MASK in the same word as a masking multiply is not seen by it: that multiply uses the previous R_MASK, and the next word sees the new one.

docs.title: Selecting a slot: mask_offset
docs.text: Each masking multiply instruction carries a 3-bit mask_offset immediate (0–7) that selects which 128-bit slot of R_MASK is used for that cycle. Eight slots can co-exist in a single loaded R_MASK value, so one load can serve eight different mask patterns per kernel.

docs.title: Deriving the active mask: mask_shift
docs.text:
Rather than using the slot mask directly, mask_shift selects from 7 derived masks generated by sequentially shifting the selected slot one bit at a time and ANDing with a partition vector after each step. Let M be the 128-bit value in the selected slot. Positive and negative shifts use different partition vectors:

mask_shift Derived mask 0 M (slot mask, unmodified) +1 (M << 1) & partition_vector +2 (derived[+1] << 1) & partition_vector +3 (derived[+2] << 1) & partition_vector −1 (M >> 1) & inverse_partition_vector −2 (derived[−1] >> 1) & inverse_partition_vector −3 (derived[−2] >> 1) & inverse_partition_vector

mask_shift names an LR register. The ctrl stage reads that register each cycle and forwards the value through the pipeline to the mult stage — the mult stage itself does not access LR registers directly. LR registers are 32-bit; negative values use 32-bit two's complement. Values outside [−3, +3] clamp to ±3.

docs.title: Partition vectors
docs.text:
Each masking multiply instruction takes a mandatory CR-index operand (cr_idx on MULT.RC.VV / MULT.RC.VE / MULT.RC.VS; dstructure_cr_idx on MULT.VE / MULT.EE, since those two already use cr_idx for the scalar multiplier) naming the CR register that supplies the dstructure configuration — there is no implicit default. Both vectors are derived from that named register's partition field (see DstructureCrIdx). The valid values of P are {0, 2, 4, 8, 16}. With partition = 0 both vectors are all-ones (no boundaries). With partition = P the 128 elements are split into P equal groups of 128 / P elements:

Vector 0-bit positions Used by partition_vector first element of each group positive shifts (+1, +2, +3) inverse_partition_vector last element of each group negative shifts (−1, −2, −3)

For partition = 2 (groups of 64):

  • partition_vector = 0 1⁶³0 1⁶³ — 0 at element 0 and element 64
  • inverse_partition_vector = 1⁶³0 1⁶³0 — 0 at element 63 and element 127

For partition = 4 (groups of 32):

  • partition_vector = 0 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹ — 0 at elements 0, 32, 64, 96
  • inverse_partition_vector = 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹0 — 0 at elements 31, 63, 95, 127

The AND at each step prevents mask bits from crossing the group boundary in either shift direction.

CR15 remains the conventional dstructure register and is set by the host harness, but it must still be named explicitly via the instruction's CR-index operand — there is no implicit fallback to CR15 (see DstructureCrIdx).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# LR1 = XMEM byte offset of mask data; CR2 = XMEM base address
LD.MASK LR1 CR2;;

# Load a vector into R0, load cyclic data into R_CYCLIC
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;;
LD.MULT.CYCLIC LR2 CR0 LR5;;

# Multiply R0 element-wise vs R_CYCLIC using slot 3, shift index in LR4, accumulate
MULT.RC.VV LR2 R0 3 LR4 CR15; ACC.ADD;;

3 is the mask_offset (slot 3 of R_MASK); LR4 holds the mask_shift index; CR15 is the dstructure register supplying partition (any CR0–CR15 may be named explicitly).

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Both examples load all-ones (0xFF…FF, 128 bits) into the selected R_MASK slot. At mask_shift = 0 every mask bit is 1, so every element is active. Each shift step clears one boundary bit to 0, deactivating one element at a time.

The tables show active elements — those whose derived mask bit is 1 and therefore contribute to accumulation.

docs.title: Example 1 — no partitioning (partition = 0)
docs.text:
With partition = 0 the partition vector is all-ones, so shifts slide freely across all 128 elements.

mask_shift Active elements (mask bit = 1) −3 0–124 −2 0–125 −1 0–126 0 0–127 (all active) +1 1–127 +2 2–127 +3 3–127

Positive shifts deactivate elements from the low end (element 0 first); negative shifts deactivate elements from the high end (element 127 first). Each step removes exactly one active element.

docs.title: Example 2 — two partitions of 64 elements each (partition = 2)
docs.text:
With partition = 2 the 128 elements are split into group 0 (elements 0–63) and group 1 (elements 64–127). Each group evolves independently and symmetrically:

  • partition_vector has 0 at element 0 and element 64 (used for positive shifts).
  • inverse_partition_vector has 0 at element 63 and element 127 (used for negative shifts).
mask_shift Group 0 active (elements 0–63) Group 1 active (elements 64–127) −3 0–60 64–124 −2 0–61 64–125 −1 0–62 64–126 0 0–63 (all) 64–127 (all) +1 1–63 65–127 +2 2–63 66–127 +3 3–63 67–127

Positive shifts deactivate elements from the start of each group (element 0 and element 64). Negative shifts deactivate elements from the end of each group (element 63 and element 127). Each step removes exactly one element per group — a perfectly symmetric sliding window.

docs.title: Jinja2 preprocessing
docs.text:
The assembler runs Jinja2 on the source when {{, {%, and {# appear.

{% set off_reg = 6 %}
SET LR0 CR{{ off_reg }};;
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;;

The harness must initialize CR6 (here: the memory offset) before this program runs.

docs.title: ABI names
docs.text:
A kernel can name its registers by role instead of by number. The assembler takes a name → register mapping (from the kernel's kernel.toml [abi] table, or ipu-as assemble --abi kernel.toml) and exposes it as two read-only namespaces: {{ cr.<name> }} renders a CR register and {{ lr.<name> }} an LR register. An unknown name is a template error at its line, and a mapping whose value is not a register of its namespace is rejected before rendering. cr and lr cannot be used as parameter or define names.

SET {{ lr.data_ptr }} {{ cr.data_base }};;
LD.MULT R0 {{ lr.data_ptr }} CR0;;

With [abi] data_base = "CR2" and data_ptr = "LR0", this renders SET LR0 CR2;;.

docs.title: Running the assembler
docs.text:
Command line (Bazel):

bazel run //src/ipu-as:ipu-as -- assemble --input prog.asm --output prog.bin

In Bazel build rules: a kernel's :assemble_<name> target writes its program (see Write a kernel); assemble_asm in src/ipu-as/defs.bzl assembles any other source.

docs.title: Configuration registers
docs.text: This page is generated from ipu_isa.constants. The host writes the CRs before a kernel runs; a kernel only reads them.

docs.title: The CRs
docs.text:
Register Value Notes CR0 0 Read-only constant. CR1 1 Read-only constant. As a scalar element it reads as 1 in every format (see CR scalars). CR2–CR15 set by the host Base addresses, strides, loop bounds, scalar constants and dstructure words. By convention CR15 holds the dstructure word, but any CR is a valid operand.

Each LR and CR holds a 32-bit scalar. A negative constant is stored as its 32-bit two's complement (value & LR_CR_SCALAR_VALUE_MASK). The element format a kernel computes in is not a CR: see Element formats.

docs.title: Dstructure word
docs.text:
A dstructure word in a CR describes the active elements of a vector. The instructions that name a dstructure CR operand (DstructureCrIdx) read it: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, AGG.MAX, AGG.MAX.FIRST, AGG.SUM, AGG.SUM.FIRST, MULT.EE, MULT.RC.VE, MULT.RC.VS, MULT.RC.VV, MULT.VE.

Field Bits Values Default valid_elements [7:0] 0–128: how many elements are active 128 partition [12:8] 0, 2, 4, 8, 16: groups of elements the MULT mask shifts within (0 is one group) 0 pad_mode [14:13] see below ZERO

The defaults are the emulator's initial CR15. Any other CR starts at 0, which decodes to valid_elements = 0.

AGG.* and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE read valid_elements; the MULT masking instructions read partition and pad_mode.

docs.title: pad_mode
docs.text:
The value a MULT masking instruction writes into the elements its mask deactivates.

Mode Code Fill value ZERO 0 0 POS_INF 1 +inf NEG_INF 2 -inf

POS_INF and NEG_INF exist only in float element formats; they are the identity values of min- and max-style reductions (ACC.MAX). In INT8 or INT32 the emulator raises EmulatorError for them.

AGG.SUM LR0 CR15;;
ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu CR3;;
MULT.RC.VV LR2 R0 0 LR4 CR15;;

docs.title: From the emulator
docs.text:
from ipu_isa.constants import LR_CR_SCALAR_VALUE_MASK, PadMode

state.regfile.set_cr(2, 0x40000)                       # a base address
state.regfile.set_cr(9, (-128) & LR_CR_SCALAR_VALUE_MASK)  # a negative constant
state.set_cr_dstructure(valid_elements=64, partition=0, pad_mode=PadMode.NEG_INF, cr_idx=3)

set_cr_dstructure writes CR15 when cr_idx is omitted.

docs.title: IPU Assembly Instruction Reference
docs.text: Per-opcode documentation is generated from InstructionDoc entries in instruction_spec.py. Operand types link to the shared operand type reference.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text:
A VLIW instruction word encodes one sub-instruction per slot. Slots are grouped into pipeline stages that execute sequentially within a cycle: CTRL (COND + LR run concurrently; LOAD address is resolved here and the data feeds MULT) → MULT → ACC → AAQ → STORE. ACC_STORE, BREAK are emulator-only: not in the hardware word. Any omitted slot is filled with NOP by the assembler automatically.

Slot Count Tag Description COND 1 HARDWARE Conditional and unconditional branches; control flow based on register comparisons. LR 3 HARDWARE Loop register instructions for controlling addresses, counters, and scalars. Three independent sub-slots per cycle. LOAD 1 HARDWARE First-stage memory loads that feed the multiply unit (mult-stage, cyclic, and mask registers). MULT 1 HARDWARE Multiply-stage instructions: element-wise and vector multiply operations. ACC 1 HARDWARE Accumulation instructions for combining multiply results into R_ACC. AAQ 1 HARDWARE Activation and quantization: apply activation to R_ACC and write quantized INT8 bytes to POST_AAQ_REG. STORE 1 HARDWARE Last-stage memory stores that drain POST_AAQ_REG to external memory after activation and quantization. ACC_STORE 1 EMULATOR Simulation-only stores of R_ACC to external memory (ST.ACC). Not implemented in real IPU hardware. BREAK 1 EMULATOR Debug break: halts execution or enters debug mode.

docs.title: NOP — No Operation
docs.text:
Syntax: NOP

Tag: HARDWARE in the hardware slots, EMULATOR in the emulator-only slots.

Faults: none (fault list).

No operation. Every slot accepts NOP. The assembler fills any omitted slot with NOP automatically. When written explicitly in a compound instruction, NOP is assigned to the next unfilled slot in compound-layout order (COND → LR → LOAD → MULT → ACC → AAQ → STORE → ACC_STORE → BREAK).

docs.title: Element formats
docs.text: The element format is selected at run time and sets the element width. Element formats lists the formats and how each encodes values.

docs.title: Compound Instruction Layout
docs.text:
The compound (VLIW) instruction word is shown two ways below, first as the hardware word, then as the emulator word.

  • Whole-word bit layout — every operand token in its actual bit position (MSB → LSB), coloured by the owning slot. This is what an encoded VLIW word looks like in memory.
  • Per-slot union layout — for each slot, the union fields packed by the layout solver, with a per-opcode grid showing which operand each opcode places in each field. Useful for seeing where cross-opcode field sharing comes from.

docs.text: The word the emulator decodes and .bin files hold: the hardware word followed by the emulator-only slots (ACC_STORE, BREAK) below its bit 0. Its top 155 bits are the hardware word.

docs.title: Conditional Branch Instructions
docs.text: Control flow instructions for branching based on conditions or unconditionally.

docs.title: BEQ — Branch if Equal
docs.text:
Syntax: BEQ reg1 reg2 label

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-2 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) reg2 LcrIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if two registers are equal.

Pseudo code: if (reg1 == reg2) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BEQ LR0 LR1 end;;
end:
HALT;;

Register reads: reg1 (LR): cycle start; reg1 (CR): cycle start; reg2 (LR): cycle start; reg2 (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: BNE — Branch if Not Equal
docs.text:
Syntax: BNE reg1 reg2 label

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-2 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) reg2 LcrIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if two registers are not equal.

Pseudo code: if (reg1 != reg2) PC = label

Example of usage: 

loop:
INC LR0 1;;
BNE LR0 CR0 loop;;

Register reads: reg1 (LR): cycle start; reg1 (CR): cycle start; reg2 (LR): cycle start; reg2 (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: BLT.S — Branch if Less Than (signed)
docs.text:
Syntax: BLT.S reg1 reg2 label

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-2 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) reg2 LcrIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if first register is less than second, as signed 32-bit integers.

Pseudo code: if (int32(reg1) < int32(reg2)) PC = label # signed 32-bit

Example of usage: 

BLT.S LR0 CR1 smaller;;
smaller:
HALT;;

Register reads: reg1 (LR): cycle start; reg1 (CR): cycle start; reg2 (LR): cycle start; reg2 (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: BGE.S — Branch if Greater or Equal (signed)
docs.text:
Syntax: BGE.S reg1 reg2 label

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-2 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) reg2 LcrIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if first register is greater than or equal to second, as signed 32-bit integers.

Pseudo code: if (int32(reg1) >= int32(reg2)) PC = label # signed 32-bit

Example of usage: 

BGE.S LR0 CR1 ge;;
ge:
HALT;;

Register reads: reg1 (LR): cycle start; reg1 (CR): cycle start; reg2 (LR): cycle start; reg2 (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: BR — Branch Register
docs.text:
Syntax: BR reg

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-2 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg LcrIdx reg: Register containing target address (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15)

General description: Branch to address in register.

Pseudo code: PC = reg

Register reads: reg (LR): cycle start; reg (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: HALT — Halt
docs.text:
Syntax: HALT

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: End the kernel after every slot of this word has retired.

Unconditional. The other slots of the same word retire first; then the kernel is done. To stop for debugging, use BREAK (emulator-only) instead. Not the host's HALT command, which stops a running kernel.

Pseudo code: no further fetch; kernel done when this word retires

Example of usage: 

HALT;;

docs.title: LR Instructions
docs.text: Loop register manipulation instructions for controlling loop counters and addresses.

docs.title: SET — Set Loop Register
docs.text:
Syntax: SET reg src

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg LrIdx reg: Loop register (LR0–LR15) src CrIdx src: Source configuration register (CR0–CR15)

General description: Copy a 32-bit value from a configuration register into a loop register.

Pseudo code: reg = cr[src]

Example of usage: 

SET LR0 CR1;;

Register reads: src (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: ADD — Add
docs.text:
Syntax: ADD dest src_a src_b

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrIdx dest: Destination local register (LR0–LR15) src_a LrIdx src_a: First source local register (LR0–LR15) src_b LcrIdx src_b: Second source — LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15

General description: Add two register sources and store the result in the destination LR.

Pseudo code: dest = src_a + src_b

Example of usage: 

ADD LR0 LR1 LR2;;
ADD LR3 LR1 CR5;;

Register reads: src_a (LR): cycle start; src_b (LR): cycle start; src_b (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: SUB — Subtract
docs.text:
Syntax: SUB dest src_a src_b

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrIdx dest: Destination local register (LR0–LR15) src_a LrIdx src_a: First source local register (LR0–LR15) src_b LcrIdx src_b: Second source — LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15

General description: Subtract the second source from the first and store the result in the destination LR.

Pseudo code: dest = src_a - src_b

Example of usage: 

SUB LR0 LR1 LR2;;
SUB LR3 LR1 CR5;;

Register reads: src_a (LR): cycle start; src_b (LR): cycle start; src_b (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: INC.MODP2 — Increment Loop Register Modulo Power of Two
docs.text:
Syntax: INC.MODP2 dest step k

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1, F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrIdx dest: Destination loop register (LR0–LR15); read and written step LcrIdx step: Signed 32-bit increment from LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15 k LrModPow2KImmediate k: Immediate in [1, 9]; encoded in 4 bits as (k − 1); mask = (1 << k) - 1

General description: Add a loop or configuration register into the destination loop register, then mask to k low bits (mod 2^k).

Pseudo code: dest <- (dest + step) & ((1 << k) - 1)

Example of usage: 

INC.MODP2 LR2 LR3 4;;

Register reads: step (LR): cycle start; step (CR): cycle start; dest (LR): cycle start.

docs.title: INC — Increment
docs.text:
Syntax: INC dest imm

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrIdx dest: Destination local register (LR0–LR15); also the implicit source imm LrIncDecImmediate imm: Unsigned immediate; range 0 to 2^W − 1 where W is derived from the LR slot union layout

General description: Add an unsigned immediate to the destination LR (read-modify-write).

Pseudo code: dest = dest + imm

Example of usage: 

INC LR0 7;;

Register reads: dest (LR): cycle start.

docs.title: DEC — Decrement
docs.text:
Syntax: DEC dest imm

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrIdx dest: Destination local register (LR0–LR15); also the implicit source imm LrIncDecImmediate imm: Unsigned immediate; range 0 to 2^W − 1 where W is derived from the LR slot union layout

General description: Subtract an unsigned immediate from the destination LR (read-modify-write).

Pseudo code: dest = dest - imm

Example of usage: 

DEC LR0 3;;

Register reads: dest (LR): cycle start.

docs.title: ADDB — Add Byte (Broadcast, Register)
docs.text:
Syntax: ADDB dest src_b

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrdIdx dest: Destination register pair (LRD0, LRD2, LRD4, ..., LRD14 — named after the lower register); LRDn = LR(n+1):LR(n), 8 byte elements; also the implicit source src_b LcrIdx src_b: LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15; low byte is read and reinterpreted as a signed two's-complement byte

General description: Broadcast-add a signed byte from an LR/CR register's low byte to each of the 8 byte elements of an LRDn register pair, saturating each element to [0, 255].

There is no separate subtract opcode: since src_b's byte is reinterpreted as signed, a value ≥ 128 (i.e. negative in two's complement) subtracts from every element instead of adding. E.g. an LR/CR whose low byte is 200 (== -56) decreases each element by 56. Because elements saturate at both ends of [0, 255], subtracting past 0 clamps at 0 rather than wrapping — it does not behave like a plain two's-complement subtract.

Pseudo code: byte_val = src_b & 0xFF # interpreted as signed int8 (two's complement) for i in 0..7: dest_byte[i] = clamp(dest_byte[i] + byte_val, 0, 255)

Example of usage: 

ADDB LRD0 LR3;;
ADDB LRD2 CR5;;

Register reads: src_b (LR): cycle start; src_b (CR): cycle start; dest (LR): cycle start.

docs.title: ADDBI — Add Byte Immediate (Broadcast)
docs.text:
Syntax: ADDBI dest imm

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrdIdx dest: Destination register pair (LRD0, LRD2, LRD4, ..., LRD14 — named after the lower register); LRDn = LR(n+1):LR(n), 8 byte elements; also the implicit source imm AddbiImmediate imm: Unsigned byte 0–255 (or an equivalent signed −128–127 literal); reinterpreted as a signed two's-complement byte for the add

General description: Broadcast-add a signed immediate byte to each of the 8 byte elements of an LRDn register pair, saturating each element to [0, 255].

There is no separate subtract opcode: write imm as a negative literal (e.g. -56) or its equivalent unsigned encoding (200) to subtract from every element instead of adding — both spellings encode the same bit pattern. Because elements saturate at both ends of [0, 255], subtracting past 0 clamps at 0 rather than wrapping — it does not behave like a plain two's-complement subtract.

Pseudo code: byte_val = imm # interpreted as signed int8 (two's complement) for i in 0..7: dest_byte[i] = clamp(dest_byte[i] + byte_val, 0, 255)

Example of usage: 

ADDBI LRD0 200;;
ADDBI LRD2 7;;

Register reads: dest (LR): cycle start.

docs.title: LOAD Instructions
docs.text: First-stage memory loads that feed the multiply unit (mult-stage registers, cyclic register, and mask register).

docs.title: LD.MULT — Load Register
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.MULT dest offset base

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1, F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest MultStageReg dest: R0 | R1 — mult-stage register to load (2-bit field; only these encodings are valid). offset LrIdx offset: LR0…LR15 — offset register, in XMEM rows. base CrIdx base: CR0…CR15 — base address register, in XMEM rows.

General description: Load data from memory into a multiplication stage register.

Pseudo code: dest = Memory[row(offset + base)] # one row = 128 elements (128 B narrow, 512 B wide-vector debug)

Example of usage: 

SET LR0 CR1;;
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;;

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; base (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: LD.MULT.CYCLIC — Load Cyclic Register
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.MULT.CYCLIC offset base index

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-4, F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details offset LrIdx offset: Offset register (LR0–LR15), in XMEM rows. base CrIdx base: Base address register (CR0–CR15), in XMEM rows. index LrIdx index: Index inside cyclic register (LR0–LR15); must hold 0, 128, 256, or 384 — the four R_CYCLIC slot boundaries, counted in elements. Any other value raises an error. All four are valid in both modes: R_CYCLIC is a 512-element ring in narrow and wide-vector debug mode alike, and a load always replaces one whole 128-element slot.

General description: Load with cyclic addressing into R_CYCLIC.

Pseudo code: R_CYCLIC[index .. index+127] = Memory[row(offset + base)] # index ∈ {0, 128, 256, 384}

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; base (CR): cycle start; index (LR): after LR writes.

docs.title: LD.MASK — Load Mask Register
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.MASK offset base

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details offset LrIdx offset: Offset register (LR0–LR15), in XMEM rows. base CrIdx base: Base address register (CR0–CR15), in XMEM rows.

General description: Load mask data from memory.

Pseudo code: R_MASK = Memory[row(offset + base) .. +128B] # reads only the row's first 128 B, in both modes -- the mask is 1 bit/element and does not scale with element width

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; base (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT Instructions
docs.text: Multiplication instructions for element-wise and element-vector operations. The multiplication result (mult_result) is forwarded to the ACC stage in the CPU and not stored in any register in the way.

docs.title: MULT.RC.VV — RC Vector × Ra Vector Multiply
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.RC.VV rc_idx ra mask_offset mask_shift cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details rc_idx LrIdx rc_idx: LR0…LR15 — base ELEMENT index into R_CYCLIC (cyclic, mod 512 elements; same unit as LD.MULT.CYCLIC's index). ra MultStageReg ra: R0 | R1 — multiplicand mult-stage register (same cycle as LD.MULT into R0/R1 is allowed). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — dstructure register supplying the partition field used to build the partition vectors and the pad_mode field used to fill deactivated elements (must be given explicitly).

General description: Multiply R_CYCLIC[rc_idx:rc_idx+128] by Ra (R0 or R1) element-wise. The partition used by mask_shift comes from cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the dstructure register's pad_mode value (zero by default, or +inf/-inf for a floating-point dtype) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: MULT_RES[i] = ipu_mult(R_CYCLIC[(rc_idx + i) % 512], ra[i]); then apply mask and shift using CR[cr_idx].partition.

Example of usage: 

MULT.RC.VV LR0 R0 0 LR2 CR15;;

Register reads: rc_idx (LR): after LR writes; ra (R): cycle start; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; R_CYCLIC: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; cr_idx (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.RC.VE — RC Vector × Scalar Multiply
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.RC.VE rc_idx src mask_offset mask_shift cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details rc_idx LrIdx rc_idx: LR0…LR15 — base ELEMENT index into R_CYCLIC (cyclic, mod 512 elements; same unit as LD.MULT.CYCLIC's index). src LcrIdx src: LR0…LR15 | CR0…CR15 — if an LR, its stored value selects the scalar from R0/R1 (0..127 → R0[idx], 128..255 → R1[idx - 128]); if a CR, its low element-width bits, decoded in the active format, are the scalar (CR1 reads as 1; see CrIdx and CR scalars). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — dstructure register supplying the partition field used to build the partition vectors and the pad_mode field used to fill deactivated elements (must be given explicitly).

General description: Multiply R_CYCLIC[rc_idx:rc_idx+128] by a scalar, element-wise. The scalar is either a single element of R0/R1 (selected by an LR value) or a CR register value. The partition used by mask_shift comes from cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the dstructure register's pad_mode value (zero by default, or +inf/-inf for a floating-point dtype) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: MULT_RES[i] = ipu_mult(R_CYCLIC[(rc_idx + i) % 512], src_value); then apply mask and shift using CR[cr_idx].partition.

Example of usage: 

MULT.RC.VE LR0 LR3 0 LR2 CR15;;

Register reads: rc_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; src (LR): after LR writes; src (CR): cycle start; R: cycle start; R_CYCLIC: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; cr_idx (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.RC.VS — RC Vector Self-Multiply (Square)
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.RC.VS rc_idx mask_offset mask_shift cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details rc_idx LrIdx rc_idx: LR0…LR15 — base ELEMENT index into R_CYCLIC (cyclic, mod 512 elements; same unit as LD.MULT.CYCLIC's index). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — dstructure register supplying the partition field used to build the partition vectors and the pad_mode field used to fill deactivated elements (must be given explicitly).

General description: Square R_CYCLIC[rc_idx:rc_idx+128] element-wise. The partition used by mask_shift comes from cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the dstructure register's pad_mode value (zero by default, or +inf/-inf for a floating-point dtype) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: rb = R_CYCLIC[(rc_idx + i) % 512]; MULT_RES[i] = ipu_mult(rb, rb); then apply mask and shift using CR[cr_idx].partition.

Example of usage: 

MULT.RC.VS LR0 0 LR2 CR15;;

Register reads: rc_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; R_CYCLIC: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; cr_idx (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.VE — Ra Vector × CR Scalar Multiply
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.VE ra_idx cr_idx mask_offset mask_shift dstructure_cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details ra_idx LrIdx ra_idx: LR0…LR15 — base element offset into combined Ra (R0 ++ R1, 256 elements, cyclic mod 256). cr_idx CrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — CR whose low element-width bits, decoded in the active format, are the scalar multiplier (CR1 reads as 1; see CrIdx and CR scalars). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). dstructure_cr_idx DstructureCrIdx dstructure_cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — dstructure register supplying the partition field used to build the partition vectors and the pad_mode field used to fill deactivated elements (must be given explicitly).

General description: Multiply Ra[ra_idx:ra_idx+128] (combined R0/R1) by a CR scalar, element-wise. The partition used by mask_shift comes from dstructure_cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the dstructure register's pad_mode value (zero by default, or +inf/-inf for a floating-point dtype) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: ra = Ra[(ra_idx + i) % 256]; MULT_RES[i] = ipu_mult(ra, CR[cr_idx][0]); then apply mask and shift using CR[dstructure_cr_idx].partition.

Example of usage: 

MULT.VE LR0 CR3 0 LR2 CR15;;

Register reads: ra_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; R: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; dstructure_cr_idx (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.EE — Ra Element × CR Scalar Multiply (broadcast)
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.EE ra_idx cr_idx mask_offset mask_shift dstructure_cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details ra_idx LrIdx ra_idx: LR0…LR15 — index of the single Ra element to read (combined R0 ++ R1, 256 elements, mod 256). cr_idx CrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — CR whose low element-width bits, decoded in the active format, are the scalar multiplier (CR1 reads as 1; see CrIdx and CR scalars). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). dstructure_cr_idx DstructureCrIdx dstructure_cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — dstructure register supplying the partition field used to build the partition vectors and the pad_mode field used to fill deactivated elements (must be given explicitly).

General description: Multiply a single Ra element by a CR scalar; broadcast the product to all 128 elements. The partition used by mask_shift comes from dstructure_cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the dstructure register's pad_mode value (zero by default, or +inf/-inf for a floating-point dtype) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: ra = Ra[ra_idx % 256]; result = ipu_mult(ra, CR[cr_idx][0]); for each element i: MULT_RES[i] = result; then apply mask and shift using CR[dstructure_cr_idx].partition.

Example of usage: 

MULT.EE LR0 CR3 0 LR2 CR15;;

Register reads: ra_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; R: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; dstructure_cr_idx (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: ACC Instructions
docs.text: Accumulation instructions for combining values with optional masking and shifting.

docs.title: ACC.ADD — Accumulate Add
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.ADD

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Running add accumulation: add multiply result into each R_ACC element.

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] += MULT_RES[i] # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.ADD;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.ADD.FIRST

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Clean-init add: overwrite each R_ACC element with the multiply result (ignores previous R_ACC).

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] = MULT_RES[i] # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.ADD.FIRST;;

docs.title: ACC.MAX — Accumulate Max
docs.text:

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Running max accumulation: each R_ACC element takes the max of its current value and the multiply result.

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] = max(R_ACC[i], MULT_RES[i]) # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.MAX;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

ACC.SUB;;

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Clean-init subtract: set each R_ACC element to the negated multiply result.

ACC.SUB.FIRST;;

docs.title: ACC.STRIDE — Accumulator Stride
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.STRIDE elements_in_row horizontal_stride vertical_stride offset

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details elements_in_row ElementsInRow elements_in_row: Elements per row (16, 32, or 64; minimum is 16) horizontal_stride HorizontalStride horizontal_stride: Horizontal stride mode (off, on, on_inv) vertical_stride VerticalStride vertical_stride: Vertical stride mode (enabled, inverted) offset LrIdx offset: LR register; value % 4 gives start index in RACC (0, 32, 64, or 96)

General description: Reorder the multiplication result into R_ACC using horizontal/vertical stride decimation. Only updates the RACC indexes written; leaves the rest unchanged.

Pseudo code: Decimate MULT_RES as rows×cols; apply horizontal stride (take every 2nd column); then vertical stride (take every 2nd row). Write result into R_ACC[start:start+N] where start = (offset%4)*32, N = 32|64|128. When a data structure has fewer than 8 elements, hardware pads to 16 automatically (not programmable).

Example of usage: 

ACC.STRIDE 16 off off LR0;;

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AGG.SUM.FIRST — Aggregate Sum (First)
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.SUM.FIRST dest_slot cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 supplying valid_elements (must be given explicitly)

General description: Sum active MULT_RES elements and write the result into R_ACC at the slot given by LR. The current value at the destination slot is NOT included in the sum (clean initialisation). Only the active element count (valid_elements) is read from cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Pseudo code: Let n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128). dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1]).

Example of usage: 

AGG.SUM.FIRST LR0 CR3;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AGG.SUM — Aggregate Sum
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.SUM dest_slot cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 supplying valid_elements (must be given explicitly)

General description: Sum active MULT_RES elements and ADD the result to R_ACC at the slot given by LR (running cross-cycle accumulation). Only the active element count (valid_elements) is read from cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Pseudo code: Let n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128). dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1]) + R_ACC[dest].

Example of usage: 

AGG.SUM LR0 CR3;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.title: AGG.MAX.FIRST — Aggregate Max (First)
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.MAX.FIRST dest_slot cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 supplying valid_elements (must be given explicitly)

General description: Find the maximum of active MULT_RES elements and write it into R_ACC at the slot given by LR. The current value at the destination slot is NOT used as a seed (clean initialisation). Only the active element count (valid_elements) is read from cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Pseudo code: Let n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128). dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1]); when n = 0 the identity seed (INT32_MIN for integer elements, -inf for float elements) is written.

Example of usage: 

AGG.MAX.FIRST LR0 CR3;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AGG.MAX — Aggregate Max
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.MAX dest_slot cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 supplying valid_elements (must be given explicitly)

General description: Find the maximum of active MULT_RES elements seeded with the current destination slot value (running cross-cycle max). Only the active element count (valid_elements) is read from cr_idx's dstructure configuration (any CR0-CR15; must be named explicitly).

Pseudo code: Let n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128). dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1], R_ACC[dest]).

Example of usage: 

AGG.MAX LR0 CR3;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.title: ACC.RESHAPE — Reshape
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.RESHAPE source dest reshape_mask

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-5 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details source LrdIdx source: LRDn register pair (LRD0, LRD2, ..., LRD14) read as source[0..7] — 8 byte elements, each a MULT_RES word index dest LrdIdx dest: LRDn register pair (LRD0, LRD2, ..., LRD14) read as dest[0..7] — 8 byte elements, each an R_ACC word index reshape_mask LrOrReshapeMaskImmediate reshape_mask: immediate 0-7 or an LR register; selects the first participating element index (elements reshape_mask..7 participate; reshape_mask = 0 uses all 8, reshape_mask = 7 uses only element 7). When an LR is given, its full value is used as the mask at runtime.

General description: Scatter MULT_RES elements into R_ACC: for each of the trailing (8 - reshape_mask) byte elements of the source/dest LRDn pairs (indices reshape_mask..7), copy MULT_RES[source[i]] to R_ACC[dest[i]].

reshape_mask skips the lowest-indexed elements 0..reshape_mask-1; the rest participate. Example: reshape_mask = 2 skips elements 0, 1; elements 2-7 participate. Example: reshape_mask = 5 skips elements 0-4; elements 5-7 participate.

Pseudo code: mult_res = MULT_RES (this cycle's MULT result) mask = reshape_mask if immediate else LR[reshape_mask] if mask > 8: raise error for i in mask..7: if source[i] >= 128 or dest[i] >= 128: raise error R_ACC[dest[i]] = mult_res[source[i]]

Example of usage: 

ACC.RESHAPE LRD0 LRD2 0;;

Register reads: source (LR): after LR writes; dest (LR): after LR writes; reshape_mask (LR): after LR writes; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AAQ Instructions
docs.text: Activation and quantization: apply activation to R_ACC elements and write quantized INT8 bytes to POST_AAQ_REG.

docs.title: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE — Activate and Quantize
docs.text:
Syntax: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE activation_fn cr_idx

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details activation_fn ActivationFn activation_fn: keyword naming the activation (one of identity, relu, relu6, sigmoid, tanh, gelu, softplus, elu, exp2, reciprocal, rsqrt, silu, window; see ACTIVATION_FN_NAMES) cr_idx DstructureCrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 supplying valid_elements (must be given explicitly)

General description: Read active elements from the forwarded R_ACC (this cycle's ACC result), apply the selected element-wise activation, clamp the results to the INT8 range [-128, 127], and write the resulting bytes to the leading active-element positions of POST_AAQ_REG; all remaining bytes are zeroed. r_acc is not modified. Requires INT8 mode. The active element count is taken from cr_idx's dstructure valid_elements field (any CR0–CR15; must be named explicitly). Available activation functions: identity (0), relu (1), relu6 (2), sigmoid (3), tanh (4), gelu (5), softplus (6), elu (7), exp2 (8), reciprocal (9), rsqrt (10), silu (11), window (12).

Pseudo code: Requires the INT8 element format (IpuState.fmt == ElementFormat.INT8). Let n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128) and k = encoded activation index. For i in [0, n): POST_AAQ_REG[i] = clamp(round(activation_k(R_ACC[i])), -128, 127). POST_AAQ_REG[n..511] = 0. R_ACC is not modified. Clamping is a placeholder until a full per-element requantize is implemented. The selector uses four bits; encodings outside the thirteen named activations behave as identity. window(x) = 1 for a <= x < b and 0 otherwise. α for elu and the window bounds a, b are not ISA operands; see docs/content/reference/isa/activate-quantize.md.

Example of usage: 

ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu CR15;;

Register reads: cr_idx (CR): cycle start; R_ACC: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: STORE Instructions
docs.text: Last-stage memory stores that drain POST_AAQ_REG to external memory after activation and quantization.

docs.title: ST.AAQ — Store Post-AAQ register
docs.text:
Syntax: ST.AAQ offset base

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details offset LrIdx offset: Offset register (LR0–LR15), in XMEM rows. base CrIdx base: Base address register (CR0–CR15), in XMEM rows.

General description: Write the whole POST_AAQ_REG to one XMEM row. Interim: after ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE it holds 128 INT8 results followed by zeros, until quantization export is finalized.

Pseudo code: Memory[row(offset + base)] = POST_AAQ_REG (the whole register, one row, in every element format)

Example of usage: 

ST.AAQ LR0 CR0;;

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; base (CR): cycle start; POST_AAQ_REG: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: Operand types
docs.text: This page is generated by ipu_gen.docs_pages from VALID_OPERAND_TYPES in instruction_spec.py and the descriptions below. For encodings per instruction, see the Instruction reference.

docs.title: ActivationFn
docs.text: AAQ-slot keyword on ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE: one of identity, relu, relu6, sigmoid, tanh, gelu, softplus, elu, exp2, reciprocal, rsqrt, silu, window (see ACTIVATION_FN_NAMES in ipu_isa.activations). Emulator-only calibration (including α and the window bounds a, b) is described in ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE in the emulator (docs/content/reference/isa/activate-quantize.md).

docs.title: AddbiImmediate
docs.text: 8-bit byte immediate for ADDBI: written as an unsigned value 0–255 or an equivalent signed -128–127 literal (both spellings encode the same bit pattern). The encoded byte is reinterpreted as a signed two's-complement int8 when broadcast-added to ADDB/ADDBI's 8 destination byte elements.

docs.title: BreakImmediate
docs.text: 16-bit value for BREAK / breakpoint slot conditions.

docs.title: CrIdx
docs.text:
Constant-register index: CR0 … CR15. CRs are read-only in assembly; the harness initializes them (e.g. base pointers, strides). CR15 conventionally holds dstructure configuration but is a valid CrIdx operand like any other CR. SET in the LR slot copies the full 32-bit CR value into an LR.

CR as an element scalar. When a CR is a multiply's scalar element operand (MULT.VE, MULT.EE, a CR src of MULT.RC.VE), the scalar is the CR's low element-width bits decoded in the active element format: the low byte in INT8 and E1–E7, all 32 bits in INT32 and FP32 (so FP32 1.0 is the CR value 0x3F800000). One rule for every format. CR0 reads as 0 and CR1 as 1 in the active format (1.0 in a float format), so a multiply by CR1 is an identity in every format; as an LR or integer operand CR1 is the integer 1.

docs.title: DstructureCrIdx
docs.text: Constant-register index: CR0 … CR15, selecting which CR supplies the valid element mask / dstructure configuration (valid_elements, partition) for AGG.SUM, AGG.SUM.FIRST, AGG.MAX, AGG.MAX.FIRST, ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, and the masking multiply instructions (MULT.RC.VV, MULT.RC.VE, MULT.RC.VS, MULT.VE, MULT.EE). Unlike CrIdx, CR15 is allowed here — it's the conventional dstructure register — but the operand is always mandatory; there is no implicit fallback to CR15 when it is omitted.

docs.title: ElementsInRow
docs.text: ACC-slot immediate: elements per row for ACC.STRIDE. Valid values: 16, 32, 64 (minimum is 16; encoded 0→16, 1→32, 2→64). See acc_stride_enums in ipu_isa.

docs.title: HorizontalStride
docs.text: ACC-slot immediate: horizontal stride mode for ACC.STRIDE. Valid values: off, on, on_inv (2-bit encoded enum; reserved3 is reserved). Expand padding is fixed hardware behaviour and is not programmable. See acc_stride_enums in ipu_isa.

docs.title: Label
docs.text: Branch target: a symbolic label or a relative offset accepted by the cond slot (e.g. loop, +3).

docs.title: LcrIdx
docs.text: LR or CR index in one field: lower indices map to LR0–LR15, higher indices to CR0–CR15 in the usual combined ordering used by the assembler. Used as src_b on ADD/SUB, as step on INC.MODP2, and as src on MULT.RC.VE (an LR's stored value selects an element from R0/R1; a CR is the scalar directly, decoded as in CrIdx).

docs.title: LrIdx
docs.text: Loop register index: resolves to LR0 … LR15. Often used for addresses, strides, and control values. When marked read: live in the spec, the emulator reads the current LR value after earlier slots in the same cycle.

docs.title: LrIncDecImmediate
docs.text: Unsigned immediate for INC / DEC in the LR slot. The bit width W is not hardcoded — it is derived from the LR slot union layout so the total slot width stays constant. Valid range: 0 to 2^W − 1.

docs.title: LrModPow2KImmediate
docs.text: Four-bit immediate for INC.MODP2: encodes exponent k with semantic k ∈ [1, 9] as (k − 1) in the word.

docs.title: LrOrReshapeMaskImmediate
docs.text: Operand on ACC.RESHAPE (bit width auto-derived from union layout): selects the first participating element slot (elements reshape_mask…7 of the source/dest LRD pair participate). Accepts either an unsigned immediate 0–7 or an LR register (its value is used directly as the mask; a resolved value greater than 8 raises an error rather than being clamped). 0 uses all 8 slots; 7 uses only slot 7; 8 uses none.

docs.title: LrdIdx
docs.text: Register-pair index: LRD0, LRD2, LRD4, … LRD14 — named after the lower register in the pair — each aliasing two adjacent LR registers as one 8-byte-element value: LRDn = LR(n+1) (high elements) concatenated with LR(n) (low elements). Purely an assembler/emulator view; there is no separate physical storage. Used as dest on ADDB / ADDBI.

docs.title: MultMaskOffsetImmediate
docs.text: Unsigned 3-bit immediate on multiply instructions: mask_offset selects slot 0–7, each a 128-bit region of R_MASK (eight mask slots total). mask_shift remains an LrIdx.

docs.title: MultStageReg
docs.text: Multiply-stage field in the VLIW encoding. Assembly accepts R0 and R1 only; the field is two bits wide (encoding 2 is reserved). Used as the destination of LD.MULT and as the ra operand of MULT.RC.VV.

docs.title: VerticalStride
docs.text: ACC-slot immediate: vertical stride bit pattern for ACC.STRIDE (see acc_stride_enums).

docs.title: Programmer's Guide: Pseudo-Instructions
docs.text: Pseudo-instructions are assembly mnemonics that the assembler expands into a real instruction at compile time. They never get an opcode and never appear in the binary, so they cost nothing at runtime — see Adding a pseudo-instruction for how they're declared. This page is generated from PSEUDO_INSTRUCTION_SPEC in instruction_spec.py.

docs.title: BGT.S — Branch if Greater Than (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BGT.S reg1 reg2 label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BLT.S (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) reg2 LcrIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if first register is greater than second.

Expands to BLT.S reg2 reg1 label at assemble time (operands swapped). Identical encoding and runtime cost to a hand-written BLT.S.

Pseudo code: if (reg1 > reg2) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BGT.S LR0 LR1 bigger;;
bigger:
HALT;;

Expands to: BLT.S reg2 reg1 label (cond slot)

docs.title: BLE.S — Branch if Less or Equal (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BLE.S reg1 reg2 label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BGE.S (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) reg2 LcrIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if first register is less than or equal to second.

Expands to BGE.S reg2 reg1 label at assemble time (operands swapped), exactly mirroring how BGT.S expands to BLT.S. Identical encoding and runtime cost to a hand-written BGE.S.

Pseudo code: if (reg1 <= reg2) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BLE.S LR0 LR1 smaller_or_equal;;
smaller_or_equal:
HALT;;

Expands to: BGE.S reg2 reg1 label (cond slot)

docs.title: BZ — Branch if Zero (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BZ reg label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BEQ (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg LcrIdx reg: Register to test (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if register is zero (CR0 is the constant 0).

Expands to BEQ reg CR0 label; CR0 is the read-only constant 0.

Pseudo code: if (reg == 0) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BZ LR0 done;;
done:
HALT;;

Expands to: BEQ reg CR0 label (cond slot)

docs.title: BNZ — Branch if Not Zero (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BNZ reg label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BNE (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg LcrIdx reg: Register to test (LR0–LR15 or CR0–CR15) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if register is not zero (CR0 is the constant 0).

Expands to BNE reg CR0 label; CR0 is the read-only constant 0.

Pseudo code: if (reg != 0) PC = label

Example of usage: 

loop:
DEC LR0 1;;
BNZ LR0 loop;;

Expands to: BNE reg CR0 label (cond slot)

docs.title: B — Unconditional Branch (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: B label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BEQ (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Always branch to label.

Expands to BEQ CR0 CR0 label. CR0 always equals itself, so the branch is always taken.

Pseudo code: PC = label

Example of usage: 

start:
INC LR0 1;;
B start;;

Expands to: BEQ CR0 CR0 label (cond slot)

docs.title: Registers
docs.text:
This page is generated from REGISTER_DEFINITIONS in ipu_isa.registers. A register with assembly names is an instruction operand; any other register is named only in the instruction reference, or is emulator storage for debugging.

Register Kind Count Bytes each Vector Assembly names R MULT 2 128 yes R0, R1 R_WIDE_DEBUG MULT 2 512 yes — R_CYCLIC MULT 1 512 yes — R_CYCLIC_WIDE_DEBUG MULT 1 2048 yes — R_MASK MULT 1 128 yes — R_ACC ACC 1 512 yes — POST_AAQ_REG AAQ 1 512 yes — LR LR 16 4 no LR0–LR15 CR CR 16 4 no CR0–CR15 MULT_RES MISC 1 512 yes — MEM_BYPASS MISC 1 128 yes —

LR and CR hold 32-bit scalars. CR0 and CR1 are read-only constants; see Configuration registers.

docs.title: IPU hardware requirements
docs.text:
The Inference Processing Unit (IPU) is a VLIW vector processor that runs neural-network kernels. Each VLIW word operates on 128-element vectors through a load, multiply, accumulate, activate-and-quantize, and store chain.

The requirements define what the IPU does and what it expects from the blocks around it. The IPU block specification and the sub-block specifications derive from the requirements.

docs.title: Specification levels
docs.text: Level Content Status 1. Requirements Goals, interfaces, main flows, faults, debug Draft 2. IPU block specification Ports, registers and timing of the IPU top Not started 3. Sub-block specifications CTRL, cache agent, MULT, ACC, AAQ, STORE, host register block Not started

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
ID Goal IPU-GOAL-1 Run every kernel in the kernel library: convolution, linear, normalization and shaping, attention, softmax, and MobileViT-S. IPU-GOAL-2 Execute one VLIW word per clock cycle while no memory access misses. IPU-GOAL-3 Close timing at 1 GHz on the TSMC 5 nm process. IPU-GOAL-4 Run consecutive kernels with no host action between them. IPU-GOAL-5 Detect every illegal state in the fault list. By default, stop with the architectural state intact and report the cause. IPU-GOAL-6 Give the host halt, single-step, breakpoints and register read-out. Later debug features extend this set without changing halt behaviour.

The kernel library is the throughput benchmark. Area and power are not constraints at this level.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Item In scope CTRL, cache agent, MULT, ACC, AAQ and STORE stages Yes Host register block and debug Yes Cache unit (CRM, XMEM, DMA) Interface and expected behaviour only RISC-V host Interface and expected software flow only ACC_STORE and BREAK ISA slots No. These slots exist in the emulator only.

docs.title: Requirement conventions
docs.text:
• Each requirement has an ID of the form IPU-<AREA>-<n>. Block specifications trace to these IDs.
  • "Shall" marks a requirement on the IPU.
  • CU-<n> marks a behaviour the IPU expects from the cache unit.
  • SW-<n> marks a behaviour the IPU expects from host software.
  • F-<n> marks a fault in the fault list.
  • OQ-<n> marks an open question. A-<n> marks an action on another document.
  • A row marked Proposed is not agreed. Open questions holds its open question.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text: Term Meaning VLIW word One instruction word. It holds one sub-instruction per slot. Slot A field of the VLIW word executed by one stage: COND, LR (three lanes), LOAD, MULT, ACC, AAQ, STORE. Kernel A program in one IMEM bank, with its CR bank and its table set. Context Context 0 or context 1. A context holds one IMEM bank, one CR bank and one table set. Active context The context the running kernel uses. The other context is the inactive context. Locked A locked context rejects host writes. Execution flow defines when a context is locked. Armed The inactive context is queued to run when the running kernel ends. Retire A word retires when the IPU has committed its last effect, including its store. Done A kernel is done when its HALT word retires. Host The RISC-V processor that loads kernels and controls the IPU. Cache unit The CRM, XMEM and DMA. It moves data between DRAM and XMEM. XMEM bank One of 16 on-chip memory banks. Each bank holds 1024 rows. Table A cache-unit data structure that maps one array to XMEM banks and DRAM. Cache agent The IPU stage that decides whether a word's memory accesses hit. Hit, miss A memory access hits when its XMEM bank is valid for the requested tag. Otherwise it misses. Halt The IPU stops at a word boundary and keeps its architectural state. Debug cause A halt cause other than a fault: halt request, step done, or breakpoint. AXI error A SLVERR response on the host port. Fault An illegal state that the IPU detects.

docs.title: Source documents
docs.text:
Document Use Instruction reference Instruction semantics and encodings Control stage specification CTRL behaviour Accumulator stage specification ACC behaviour AaQ and store stage specification AAQ and STORE behaviour Cache unit specification CRM, XMEM and DMA behaviour

Open questions lists the conflicts between these documents.
